articles.title: Construction Industry Continues to Face Engineering Challenges in Chalk Foundation Design
articles.excerpt: At a recent geotechnical lecture hosted in London, experts discussed ongoing industry challenges and lessons learned regarding chalk foundation design.
articles.content: Recent discussions at a prominent geotechnical lecture in London highlighted the ongoing complexities and recurring disputes associated with chalk foundations in the built environment. Delivering the annual address, geotechnical specialist Chris Raison noted that despite extensive research and published technical literature, the construction sector regularly encounters challenges related to chalk bedrock. The primary issue stems from misconceptions regarding the material itself, whereas problems are frequently driven by material absence, weathering, or alterations caused by natural and human activities. Weathering can significantly diminish the density, strength, and stiffness of chalk, while dissolution features introduce difficult-to-assess weak zones. Reviewing historical case studies from past decades, the presentation demonstrated how geological and geotechnical risks directly impact the execution and long-term behavior of pile foundations. Experts emphasized that technical guidance is not always applied consistently across various projects. Understanding site-specific ground conditions remains critical for engineers to prevent construction delays, cost escalations, and contractual disputes. Thorough preliminary investigations and careful consideration of geological risks during design and construction are essential for delivering resilient and successful foundation solutions across similar geologic environments.
articles.originalTitle: Industry still has lessons to learn about chalk foundations - New Civil Engineer

articles.title: Art Institute of Chicago Restitutes Nazi-Era Painting to Heirs
articles.excerpt: The Art Institute of Chicago has agreed to restitute a 1913 painting by Jean Metzinger, sold in Nazi-occupied Amsterdam, to the heirs of Emanuel Lewenstein.
articles.content: The Art Institute of Chicago has agreed to return Jean Metzinger's 1913 painting Woman With a Fan to the heirs of Emanuel Lewenstein. According to Jacques Schuhmacher, the museum's head of provenance research, the painting was sold under pressure during an October 1940 auction in Amsterdam following the Nazi invasion. The artwork belonged to Lewenstein, a Jewish art collector whose family faced persecution, and was deposited at the Stedelijk Museum for safekeeping before the family emigrated. The Art Institute of Chicago acquired the painting in 1959 from a New York gallery. Provenance researchers utilized infrared photography to examine faint pencil marks on the reverse of the canvas, identifying dealer Paul Citroen and establishing the connection to the Lewenstein family. Officials praised the institution's cooperative restitution process. In a separate legal development concerning the same museum, a New York appeals court ruled that the Manhattan district attorney's office improperly used penal code provisions to seize an Egon Schiele drawing, stating that criminal law is unsuitable for resolving complex ownership disputes.
articles.originalTitle: Art Institute of Chicago restitutes Metzinger painting sold in Nazi-occupied Amsterdam - The Art Newspaper

articles.title: Skanska to Lead the Comprehensive Rehabilitation of a Landmark Potomac River Bridge
articles.excerpt: A historic bridge crossing the Potomac River between Washington, D.C. and Virginia is slated for a major rehabilitation project.
articles.content: Constructed in the mid-twentieth century, the historic four-lane bridge crossing the Potomac River between Washington, D.C. and Arlington, Virginia, is scheduled for a significant rehabilitation initiative. Led by Skanska USA Civil alongside engineering partners, the design-build project commissioned by local transport authorities aims to extend the operational lifespan of the structure by seventy-five years. Operations are set to commence next year with a projected completion date in the fall of 2029. Key engineering interventions include upgrading vessel protection systems to meet contemporary collision standards, rehabilitating superstructure and substructure elements, and replacing secondary components such as drainage networks and signage. To minimize disruption for the heavy daily volume of motorists, accelerated bridge construction techniques will be employed to convert the existing movable span into a permanent fixed structure. The new span will be constructed adjacent to the current alignment and maneuvered into position during a restricted weekend closure. Jointly funded by transportation authorities and federal highway administration bodies, the initiative forms part of a broader regional effort to modernize critical transportation corridors connecting the capital district and neighboring states, thereby ensuring long-term structural integrity and transport continuity.
articles.originalTitle: Skanska To Lead Rehab of Landmark Potomac River Bridge - Engineering News-Record

articles.title: Gray Wielebinski Exhibition in London Examines Masculinity and Consumer Culture
articles.excerpt: Gray Wielebinski's exhibition at Nicoletti in London explores the construction of masculinity through found ephemera and consumer culture references.
articles.content: Nicoletti in London presents Gray Wielebinski's exhibition, Bring Me Men. The artist's sculptural objects and box installations utilize found ephemera, magazine clippings, and consumer artifacts to examine how masculine identities are constructed through visual culture. Incorporating materials such as paper shopping bags, literary references to Truman Capote and Yukio Mishima, and personal mementos, the works evoke the private spaces of adolescence and the curation of queer desires. The vitrines and wall-mounted drawer pieces contrast idealized depictions of athletic male bodies with textual interventions that reference bullying and societal stereotypes. Drawing upon trans identity and personal history, the collage works investigate the fluid processes through which identity is shaped over a lifetime. The exhibition was on view at the gallery from May 28 to July 4.
articles.originalTitle: Gray Wielebinski: Unboxing Queer Desires - ArtReview

articles.title: Digital Art Pioneer John Gerrard Examines Touchscreens and the Future of Art
articles.excerpt: Artist John Gerrard discusses his virtual worlds built with game-engine technology, his SPIRITS project hosted by LACMA, and the future of digital networks.
articles.content: Artist John Gerrard explores real-time virtual worlds and simulations centered on energy, power, and ecology. Utilizing game-engine technology, the artist developed the SPIRITS project, which has unfolded across the Los Angeles County Museum of Art platform in four movements since the winter of 2025. Transforming lost plastic shoes found on various shores into three-dimensional digital images via Gaussian splats, the project allows viewers to spin variable stories by touching their screens. As the final chapter goes live on lacma.org, the artist reflects on the potentials of our networked age and the power of digital touch. Noting that the electromagnetic relationship between finger and screen fosters a deep connection unlike standard two-dimensional media, Gerrard highlights growing tensions between physical spaces and digital networks. Emphasizing that artificial intelligence cannot fully replace human labor, the artist points out that hand-crafted coding and iterative processes remain essential for perception and experience. Achieving the desired qualities requires weeks of work, while art token mechanisms provide a structured foundation for digital art communities. Observing that collectors are increasingly drawn to both digital art and these mechanisms, Gerrard anticipates that galleries and institutions will continue adapting to these shifts. Asserting that physical gathering points and digital networks will coexist in the future, the artist supports this transition through his ongoing role as a system thinker at the Van Abbemuseum.
articles.originalTitle: Are touchscreens the next art frontier? Digital pioneer John Gerrard thinks so - Art Basel

articles.title: Mauritshuis Museum Restitutes Seventeenth Century Painting Looted During the Nazi Era
articles.excerpt: The Mauritshuis has decided to return a seventeenth century Dutch painting to the heirs of Jewish art dealer Jacques Goudstikker following provenance research.
articles.content: The Mauritshuis has decided to return a seventeenth century Dutch painting to the heirs of Jewish art dealer Jacques Goudstikker following provenance research. The 1651 work by Jan van Goyen had been acquired by the museum in 1967. Following Goudstikker's death while fleeing to England in 1940, his gallery's artworks were transported without consent and sold into the collection of Hermann Göring. Dutch Culture Minister Rianne Letschert agreed to follow formal advice from the Restitutions Committee to return the work to the widow of Goudstikker's only son. The committee stated that the loss of possession was involuntary and consistent with Nazi authorities forcing sales while giving them an appearance of legality. This decision forms part of a policy shift in Dutch restitution practices toward greater transparency and goodwill regarding Nazi looted art. Museum representatives noted that the artwork left the collection unjustly and returning it was the correct course of action.
articles.originalTitle: Mauritshuis to restitute 17th-century Dutch painting after research reveals it belonged to renowned Jewish dealer - The Art Newspaper

articles.title: Construction Industry Introduces a New Joint Code of Practice to Support Workforce Mental Health
articles.excerpt: A newly released joint code of practice seeks to address workforce wellbeing and mental health challenges across the construction sector.
articles.content: Professionals within the civil engineering and infrastructure sectors face unique occupational pressures, including extended working hours, extensive travel demands, and rigorous deadlines that contribute to significant psychological stress. Emphasizing that workforce wellbeing is a collective responsibility, industry authorities have welcomed the new Mental Health in Construction Joint Code of Practice issued by the Construction Leadership Council. Statistical data revealing disproportionately elevated rates of psychological distress and suicide among construction personnel underscore the urgent need for a coordinated industry response. Because the built environment sector comprises an interconnected network of clients, consultants, contractors, and suppliers, meaningful reform requires standardized frameworks adopted across all organizational tiers. The newly established code prioritizes preventive measures rather than reactive interventions, identifying five core domains that influence employee wellbeing: working patterns, operational demands, workplace culture, financial pressures, and accessibility of support services. Professional institutions continue to promote member welfare through dedicated benevolent funds and advisory resources. By embedding these shared principles into daily operations, organizations aim to foster an open, supportive culture that reduces stigma and ensures comprehensive assistance is readily available to personnel navigating challenging circumstances.
articles.originalTitle: Mental health in construction: a collective responsibility - New Civil Engineer

articles.title: Vogue World Event Inside the Milan Galleria Celebrates Italian Craftsmanship
articles.excerpt: Following international stops, the event held in Milan's Galleria showcases custom runway designs and collaborations honoring Italy's rich history of artisanal craft, innovative textile technologies, and cinematic heritage.
articles.content:
Following stops in New York, London, Paris, and Los Angeles, Vogue World arrived in Milan with a special event held inside the historic Galleria. Taking place in the heart of the city, the evening featured archival and custom runway designs paying homage to Italy's history of artisanal craft, textile technology, and forward-thinking ideas, alongside a special collaboration with the Teatro alla Scala Chorus. Francesca Ragazzi, Vogue Italia's head of editorial content, stated in a release that the event offers a unique opportunity to celebrate the story of Italian craftsmanship in the era of artificial intelligence.

Juan Costa Paz, the creative director for the presentation, noted that Milan serves as a hub for craftsmanship and that the narrative was expressed through fashion. The opening of the show featured three objects commissioned by curator Judith Clark: a model of the Duomo, a celestial sphere, and a loom. These objects represent the combination of hand and machine and Italy's artisanal heritage. The first act focused on Renaissance-inspired textiles, while the second act drew inspiration from the industrial revolution of Torino with tailored silhouettes. The final act celebrated color and the cinematic mythology of the golden age of Italian cinema.
articles.originalTitle: What Is Vogue World: Milano? Your First Look at the Fashion and Craftsmanship Behind the Show - Vogue

articles.title: Landmark Paris Exhibition at the Grand Palais Explores Paul Cezanne’s Enduring Influence Across Generations
articles.excerpt: The Grand Palais in Paris hosts an unprecedented exhibition examining Paul Cezanne's profound impact on countless artists, from Pablo Picasso to Peter Doig.
articles.content: The Grand Palais in Paris is hosting a landmark exhibition dedicated to Paul Cezanne, resulting from an unprecedented collaboration between the Centre Pompidou, the Musée d'Orsay, and the Musée de l'Orangerie. Curated by Jean-Rémi Touzet, the presentation moves beyond a straightforward retrospective to trace the French master's impact on contemporaries and subsequent generations of painters. The exhibition features 70 works by Cezanne, largely drawn from the collections of the Musée d'Orsay and the Musée de l'Orangerie, displayed alongside 75 works by diverse artists such as André Derain, Wolfgang Tillmans, Joan Mitchell, Zao Wou-Ki, Etel Adnan, Henri Matisse, Max Beckmann, Piet Mondrian, and Kazimir Malevich. Historical accounts often point to the Salon d'Automne of 1907 as the moment of critical breakthrough, yet contemporaries like Paul Gauguin and Émile Bernard closely engaged with his technique during the artist's lifetime. Structured chronologically and thematically, the exhibition explores central leitmotifs including landscapes, still lifes, and bather scenes. Notable loans include The Bather from the Museum of Modern Art in New York, presented in dialogue with Peter Doig's Bather. Mountain ridge paintings of Sainte-Victoire and works by Fabienne Verdier and Mark Tansey further illuminate Cezanne's complex legacy.
articles.originalTitle: Paul Cezanne’s influence on generations of artists laid bare in Parisian exhibition - The Art Newspaper

articles.title: Machine Learning Models for Converting Biomedical Waste into Energy
articles.excerpt: A new study explores the use of hybrid machine learning models to predict and optimize product distributions during the processing of biomedical waste. The research evaluates the effects of process parameters on product yields.
articles.content:
Biomedical waste generated by hospitals, clinics, and laboratories, including syringes and tissue samples, poses significant environmental and public health challenges when not handled properly. Traditional disposal methods can lead to secondary pollution. A study published in the Journal of Hazardous, Toxic, and Radioactive Waste explores converting this waste into valuable materials and energy-dense products such as bio-oil, syngas, and biochar through chemical heat energy processes. Optimizing yield and quality presents a scientific and engineering challenge due to the wide variety of waste.

Researchers proposed and evaluated hybrid machine learning models, specifically XGBoost and LightGBM, to predict product distributions from thermochemical processes. Combining literature-derived data with lab-scale experimental results, the authors developed a practical decision support system. Based on a compiled dataset of 180 points, the proposed hybrid model achieved high classification accuracy for process selection. Feature importance and sensitivity analyses indicated that temperature, catalyst concentration, and residence time are the dominant factors influencing product yields.
articles.originalTitle: Machine learning can help convert biomedical waste to usable energy products - American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)

articles.title: Sustainable Student Residence and Academic Facility Completed in Toronto
articles.excerpt: Designed in collaboration between Dutch architecture firm Mecanoo and RDHA, the Lawson Centre for Sustainability at Trinity College in Toronto spans 14,450 square meters using hybrid mass timber construction.
articles.content: Constructed for Trinity College in Canada, the Lawson Centre for Sustainability represents the institution's most substantial capital project in over six decades. Designed by Mecanoo in collaboration with RDHA, the 14,450-square-meter academic and residential facility revitalizes the campus while embodying the college's rigorous environmental commitments. The complex accommodates a 357-bed student dormitory alongside academic offices, seminar rooms, a cafeteria, an event pavilion, and a rooftop agricultural farm. Achieving LEED Platinum and CaGBC Zero Carbon design certifications, the building features an advanced hybrid mass timber structure. Structural engineering was provided by Blackwell Structural Engineers, with Smith + Andersen handling MEP and HVAC consultancy, and Footprint Consulting advising on sustainability. Built under the construction management of Graham Construction, the development establishes elevated ecological standards for student housing and academic infrastructure in Toronto.
articles.originalTitle: Trinity College Lawson Centre for Sustainability / Mecanoo + RDHA - ArchDaily

articles.title: Exhibition at Lever House Explores Collaboration Between Isamu Noguchi and Gordon Bunshaft
articles.excerpt: Recently opened at Lever House in New York, a new exhibition examines the creative partnership and sculptural proposals between artist Isamu Noguchi and architect Gordon Bunshaft.
articles.content: The iconic Lever House in Midtown Manhattan, New York, is currently hosting a comprehensive exhibition dedicated to the works of Isamu Noguchi. Organized in collaboration with the Noguchi Museum, the exhibition explores the enduring creative partnership between the artist and architect Gordon Bunshaft, one of the building's principal designers. Featuring over a dozen sculptures distributed throughout the lobby and outdoor plazas, the showcase highlights the aesthetic compatibility between Noguchi's organic forms and the rigid structural language of corporate modernism. The display also presents scale models, architectural drawings, and archival materials documenting unrealized landscape and sculpture garden proposals developed for the site. These representational artifacts bring to light a subtle humanism embedded within Bunshaft's architectural framework. Remaining on view through the summer months at the Park Avenue landmark, the exhibition commemorates the historic synergy between two prominent creative figures.

articles.title: Subsea Habitat Installed off Florida Keys Establishes Benchmark for Future Projects
articles.excerpt: International engineering firm DEEP has successfully installed Vanguard, a new subsea research habitat, on the seabed within the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary. Serving as a pilot structure, the deployment sets a technical precedent for future modular underwater habitats.
articles.content: International ocean engineering and technology company DEEP has anchored its Vanguard subsea habitat to the seabed approximately 4.5 miles off the Florida Keys. Situated at a depth of roughly sixty feet near the Tennessee Reef within a national marine sanctuary, the four-person facility is designed to support advanced marine research and saturation diving operations. Prior to installation, comprehensive bathymetric, geotechnical, and biological surveys were conducted in coordination with federal sanctuary authorities to ensure environmental preservation. Constructed primarily from an existing industrial decompression chamber, the facility integrates living quarters, science workstations, and a wet porch featuring a moon pool for diver access. To withstand extreme meteorological events such as Category 5 hurricanes, the structure is secured by a 220-ton steel base plate anchored with deep steel piles driven into the underlying limestone. Currently undergoing final commissioning by maritime certification body DNV, Vanguard functions as a foundational pilot test for anticipated larger-scale and modular subsea infrastructure projects in the future.
articles.originalTitle: Underwater habitat off Florida Keys sets stage for more ambitious projects - American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)

articles.title: Alexander McQueen Returns to Its Roots and Dark Aesthetic at London Fashion Week
articles.excerpt: Departing from the Paris schedule, the Alexander McQueen brand showcased its spring summer 2027 collection in a 17th-century underground chapel during London fashion week. Amid a restructuring process, the fashion house focused on Tommy Nutter's radical tailoring and British references.
articles.content: Departing from the Paris schedule, the Alexander McQueen brand showcased its spring summer 2027 collection in a 17th-century subterranean London chapel during London fashion week. Featuring steel harnesses, bulky ankle-strapped heels resembling electronic monitoring tags, and a chain mail dress made of tiny silver skulls, the presentation recalled the brand's daring historical shows. As the label undergoes a challenging restructuring process involving store closures and job losses under the leadership of chief executive Gianfranco d'Attis, returning to London marked a strategic homecoming. The business strategy aims to streamline the brand by reducing trainers and sweatshirts while refocusing on evening gowns and British tailoring. Creative director Seán McGirr drew inspiration for the vaulted undercroft venue from Piero della Francesca's painting. Jackets paid homage to Tommy Nutter's radical tailoring, while hair designs referenced rave culture. The designer noted that London's unconventional street style served as constant stimulation. By incorporating organza into meringue-like peaks on the shoulders of an ivory lace dress, he sought to transform the famous exaggerated silhouettes into angel wings with an ethereal and light message. Concurrently, Roksanda Ilinčić presented a contrasting sunny showcase at a rooftop garden near the National Theatre, featuring thick plaited rope belts celebrating the monumental fabric sculptures of Françoise Grossen alongside cherry and lavender silk garments.
articles.originalTitle: McQueen comes home to happy, dark place at London fashion week | Alexander McQueen - The Guardian

articles.title: Hiroshi Sugimoto Exhibits Works That Suspend Time in New York
articles.excerpt: Hiroshi Sugimoto's exhibition at Lisson Gallery in New York brings together photographs from his diorama series and new washi paper folding screens.
articles.content: Lisson Gallery in New York presents Hiroshi Sugimoto's third solo exhibition, titled Unnatural Habitat. Running from September 15 to October 24, 2026, the exhibition traces a fifty-year dialogue between the artist and the city, exploring perceptions of time and reality. The presentation features works from Sugimoto's Diorama series, including photographs created through recent access to the American Museum of Natural History collections, newly enlarged negatives, and color diorama photographs printed on washi paper as traditional Japanese byōbu folding screens. Inspired by artificial habitats encountered in 1975, the diorama works examine the tension between preserving a constructed reality and transforming it photographically. Produced using Kyoto craftsmanship, the washi screens introduce a rare use of color into Sugimoto's practice while giving the images a distinct sculptural presence. The exhibition coincides with a major solo presentation at the Singapore Art Museum and precedes the reopening of the Hirshhorn Sculpture Garden.
articles.originalTitle: Hiroshi Sugimoto: Unnatural Habitat - Artguide

articles.title: Aluminium Shingle Pavilion Debuts as Experimental Structure at Art Omi
articles.excerpt: US studio MOS Architects has completed an egg-shaped experimental pavilion covered in aluminium shingles at the Art Omi campus in New York. Drawing inspiration from pre-modern basketry and mid-century futurism, the structure provides a unique shelter and rest space within the landscape.
articles.content: The recently installed experimental pavilion at the Art Omi arts center in Upstate New York explores alternative material applications and smaller-scale architectural expressions. Designed by MOS Architects, the egg-shaped structure features an ultra-thin shell composed of overlapping aluminium shingles secured with stainless steel bolts. Drawing conceptual cues from traditional woven basketry and mid-century travel trailers, the pavilion rests on stilts and includes multiple oculi that frame views of the surrounding landscape while offering a shaded place of rest. According to the studio co-founder, the project serves as a deliberate counter-response to prevailing commercial pressures within contemporary architecture, emphasizing instead the experimental freedom found in compact installations. Built to be assembled rapidly using standard tools, the project highlights the lightweight and efficient structural potential of folded metallic components within an open-air exhibition context.
articles.originalTitle: MOS creates basket-like aluminium pavilion at Art Omi in New York - Dezeen
